results.title: Banana chips brand Beyond Snack bags $8.3 million in round led by 12 Flags Group - The Economic Times
results.content:
Kerala-based banana chips brand Beyond Snack has raised $8.3 million in a funding round led by consumer business-focused fund 12 Flags Group.  
  
The round also saw participation from Japanese venture capital firm Enrission India Capital and existing investors like Faad Network and agriculture and food-focused early stage fund Nab Ventures.   
  
The funds will be used for expanding into new markets, driving product innovation, and enhancing its supply chain infrastructure.  
  
“Last year, we were just starting out with distribution. Now, around 50% of our revenue is coming from retail, which means our distribution has become much stronger than it was a year ago. Moving forward, we will continue to drive our retail growth even further,” founder Manas Madhu told ET. [...] While the startup is concentrating on expanding its footprint in India, it is also exploring new international markets. Currently operating in 12 countries, its key markets include the US, Australia, New Zealand, and Dubai.  
  
Its products are also available on ecommerce and quick commerce platforms, with around 40% of its revenue coming from quick commerce channels. Madhu noted that the company has doubled its revenue from FY23 to FY24 and aims to achieve the same growth for FY25, driven by the expansion in retail and quick commerce.  
  
It last raised $3.5 million in funding from the National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (Nabard)-backed Nab Ventures in July 2023. [...] BenchmarksCLOSED

results.title: Banana Chips: A Global Snack with Cultural Roots and Modern Appeal
results.content:
The global banana chips market is witnessing robust expansion, driven by the increasing demand for fruit-based snacks that offer convenient, nutrient-rich alternatives to traditional processed snacks. Valued at approximately USD 1.5 billion in 2025, the market is projected to reach USD 2.04 billion by 2030, growing at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 6.34%. This growth is fueled by shifting consumer preferences toward healthier indulgences, with banana chips benefiting from their natural fruit base, portability, and versatility in flavors from classic salted to innovative spiced variants. [...] ### Regional Market Trends

North America: The North American banana chips market is valued at around USD 450 million in 2025 and is projected to grow at a CAGR of 5.2%. Growth is primarily driven by the rising demand for low-calorie and baked variants due to obesity concerns affecting approximately 42% of adults. Fusion flavors, such as chili-lime and matcha are gaining popularity in urban centers, with imports from the Philippines and Ecuador increasing by 15% year over year. Retailers like Whole Foods emphasize organic and clean-label lines, while e-commerce platforms report a 25% increase in sales of health-focused packs. Despite competition from local potato chips, innovations such as vacuum-fried options position banana chips as a healthier snack alternative. [...] Asia-Pacific: The Asia-Pacific region dominates global banana chip consumption, holding over 50% market share, with a CAGR of 7.5% and a market valuation of USD 750 million in 2025. Cultural integration, rapid urbanization and rising middle-class incomes drive strong demand for both traditional deep fried and spiced export-oriented variants. Key producers like India and the Philippines account for 60% of the volume, while countries such as China and Indonesia experience 35% growth in spiced, export-focused packs. Climate-resilient varieties and local sourcing strategies reduce supply risks, supporting a 25% increase in exports to Western markets. Mature markets focus on innovation and sustainability, while emerging markets capitalize on volume and affordability.

results.content:
The global banana chips market stood at $1.9 billion in 2025 and reaches $3.21 billion by 2034, a compound annual growth rate of 6.0% that adds $1.31 billion of annual sales over the period. The value covers sweetened chips coated in sugar, honey or jaggery and unsweetened chips that are salted, spiced or plain, made from Saba, Cardaba, Nendran and other cooking bananas and sold at retail or in bulk to food manufacturers. Plantain chips marketed as a separate category, banana flour, banana flakes and dried whole banana sit outside this perimeter, although they share growers and processors with chip makers and track the same raw material cycle as the wider banana market. The global banana chips market stood at $1.9 billion in 2025 and reaches $3.21 billion by 2034, a compound annual growth rate of 6.0% that adds $1.31 billion of annual sales over the period. The value covers sweetened chips coated in sugar, honey or jaggery and unsweetened chips that are salted, spiced or plain, made from Saba, Cardaba, Nendran and other cooking bananas and sold at retail or in bulk to food manufacturers. Plantain chips marketed as a separate category, banana flour, banana flakes and dried whole banana sit outside this perimeter, although they share growers and processors with chip makers and track the same raw material cycle as the wider banana market. [...] ## Banana Chips Market by Type

Unsweetened chips hold 57.0% of global banana chips value in 2025 and grow at 6.2% a year to 2034. This segment is anchored by Kerala's salted Nendran chips, fried in coconut oil and sold everywhere from roadside chip shops to supermarket shelves, along with spicy and masala variants and plain chips. Indian consumption is the largest single block of unsweetened demand, and it commands high retail prices: native chips reached up to INR 440 per kg in Kerala ahead of Onam 2026. The segment grows faster than sweetened chips because branded Indian players are converting loose sales into packaged products.

results.title: Beyond Snack reports 55% revenue surge to Rs 53 crore in FY25 | Priyanka Araballi posted on the topic | LinkedIn
results.content: Banana chips brand Beyond Snack reported a 55% surge in revenue to Rs 53 crore in FY25, up from Rs 34.2 crore in FY24, according to its financial statements sourced from the Registrar of Companies (RoC). Revenue from product sales stood at Rs 52 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 33.7 crore in FY24. The company also recorded Rs 1 crore in other income, primarily from interest on fixed deposits in FY25, up from Rs 50 lakh in FY24. On the expenditure side, total expenses rose sharply by 82% to Rs 73.8 crore in FY25, from Rs 40.5 crore in FY24. The largest cost component, cost of goods sold, increased by 58% to Rs 32.9 crore in FY25, compared to Rs 20.9 crore in FY24. Employee benefit expenses nearly doubled to Rs 9.6 crore from Rs 5 crore in FY24. Finance costs and depreciation remained [...] Rs 5 crore in FY24. Finance costs and depreciation remained relatively modest at Rs 50 lakh and Rs 1.1 crore, respectively, in FY25. Advertising expenses witnessed a significant 2.3X jump to Rs 8.3 crore in FY25, up from Rs 3.7 crore in FY24. The company reported a net loss of Rs 20.9 crore in FY25, marking a 3.3X increase from Rs 6.3 crore in FY24. On a unit economics basis, Beyond Snack spent Rs 1.42 to earn every rupee of revenue in FY25, compared to Rs 1.20 in FY24. Beyond Snack is an Indian snacking company specializing in premium, Kerala-style banana chips. Founded in 2020 and headquartered in Alappuzha, Kerala, the brand gained nationwide recognition after its appearance on Shark Tank India Season 1, where it secured investment from Ashneer Grover and Aman Gupta.
